G1.name: Gradient variance (barren-plateau onset G1, depth retention G2)
G1.unit: variance of one finite-difference cost derivative over random angles
G1.source: McClean et al., Nat. Commun. 9, 4812 (2018); Cerezo et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 1791 (2021); definitions per Larocca et al. 2025
deviations: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. The gradient is checked against PennyLane autodiff on all four families (the finite difference agrees to its O(step**2) error), and A1's onset slope reproduces the old HEA value (alpha ~ 0.71). The cross-family onset slopes are not yet checked against a published curve.

The derivative is a central finite difference, not a two-term parameter shift: the two-term shift is exact only for Pauli rotations and is wrong for A4's controlled CRZ gates (checked: off by ~7%). See probes.gradient.
The variance is averaged over N_ANGLES angles spread across the circuit, not one fixed angle. A single angle can be exactly degenerate at shallow depth (zero gradient), which the average removes.

Depth and width are swept independently, unlike the old code which tied d = n for G1. The onset slope is therefore fitted at a fixed depth; the d = n diagonal is available in the grid if that comparison is wanted.
The shot floor 1/1024 is a convention carried from the old scorecard, not a measured or analytic value.

G5.name: Noise-induced barren plateau (gradient variance under depolarizing noise)
G5.unit: variance of one finite-difference cost derivative over random angles, per noise level
G5.source: Wang et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 6961 (2021); closed form per Larocca et al. 2025, Box 8
deviations: PER-GATE NOISE, NOT PER-LAYER. The source model is one local Pauli channel per layer; here a DepolarizingChannel(p) follows every gate, because 'layer' is not the same object across the four families. Gate-heavy circuits are therefore noisier at equal (n, d) - the coupling to P6 is deliberate and NISQ-faithful. The depth decay remains exponential; only the effective rate changes.
Depolarizing only. Bit-flip and phase-flip channels are not swept.
The rotation angles are noiseless and there is no readout or shot noise; the simulation is analytic on a density matrix.
p_crit is interpolated between swept noise levels (log-log), and an uncrossed floor is reported as None, never as a robustness score - both fixes to defects named on the old G5 slide.
The angle pool is 3 indices, not G1's 6, to bound the density-matrix cost. The p = 0 column must match G1; that agreement is a test.

G6.name: Initialisation sensitivity (gradient second moment and QFIM rank vs init scale)
G6.unit: E[(dC)^2] of one finite-difference cost derivative, and QFIM rank, per initialisation scale a
G6.source: Haug, Bharti & Kim, PRX Quantum 2, 040309 (2021); Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv:2203.09376); first-step caveat per Grant et al., Quantum 3, 214 (2019)
deviations: A FIXED RANDOM PRODUCT PRE-LAYER precedes the ansatz and a FIXED POST-LAYER follows it (seeded Rot per wire, derived from family/n/d). Without the pre-layer, |0...0> is a maximum of both package costs and the small-angle derivative vanishes by construction - the design fault of the old G6. Without the post-layer, the theta = 0 circuit of a rotation-plus-CNOT family is Clifford, the Z-string cost stays diagonal, and every Z-generator gradient is exactly zero - so the post-layer measures the same cost in a fixed random local basis, as Zhang et al.'s trailing RX/RY layers do. Both are fixed local unitaries: they move the start state and the basis, not the geometry.

The reported gradient quantity is the SECOND MOMENT E[(dC)^2], not the variance: at small scale the mean derivative is nonzero, so the variance alone would under-read trainability. At a = 1 the mean vanishes by symmetry and the second moment equals G1's variance.
Scales are drawn as theta = a * U[0, 2*pi), Haug's protocol, rather than the N(0, sigma^2) of Zhang; Zhang's sigma^2 = O(1/L) guarantee is quoted on the definition slide but the swept variable is a.
The QFIM rank uses P3's probe and threshold at RANK_POINTS base points per scale, not P3's full 30-point protocol; the a = 1 column is checked against P3 in the tests.
Identity-block initialisation (Grant 2019) is cited, not implemented.

P1.name: Expressibility (KL divergence against Haar)
P1.unit: nats, 0 = indistinguishable from Haar, larger = less uniform coverage
P1.source: Sim, Johnson & Aspuru-Guzik, Adv. Quantum Technol. 2, 1900070 (2019)
deviations: The Haar term is integrated exactly per bin through the cumulative form, not read at bin centres. This is more accurate than the reference implementation.
The estimator is positively biased at finite pair count. Compare every value against kl_haar_floor before reading it as physics.
A fixed unitary at the end of a circuit cancels inside the fidelity, so P1 is blind to a terminal entangling layer.
The encoder input is held fixed, so P1 describes the ansatz and not the encoder.

P2.name: Entangling capability (Meyer-Wallach)
P2.unit: dimensionless, 0 = product state, 1 = every qubit maximally mixed
P2.source: Meyer & Wallach, J. Math. Phys. 43, 4273 (2002); Brennen, QIC 3, 619 (2003); averaging protocol from Sim et al., Adv. Quantum Technol. 2, 1900070 (2019)
deviations: The reference is the analytic Haar expectation at each n. The old scorecard used 0.4 at every n, which is the correct value at n = 2 only; the true value rises towards 1 as n grows.
Q uses single-qubit reduced states only, so it cannot distinguish GHZ from W type entanglement.
The encoder input is held fixed, so P2 describes the ansatz and not the encoder.

P3.name: Effective dimension (QFIM rank)
P3.unit: count of independent parameter directions; ceiling min(p, 2^(n+1)-2)
P3.source: Haug, Bharti & Kim, PRX Quantum 2, 040309 (2021); over-parameterisation reading from Larocca et al., Quantum 7, 1116 (2023)
deviations: The Jacobian of the state is a central finite difference with step 1e-3, not an exact parameter shift. The O(step**2) error is near 1e-6 and is validated against a closed-form single-rotation QFIM in the tests.
The rank uses a fixed relative threshold of 1e-5 on the QFIM spectrum. Report the threshold with any rank, because a rank is threshold-defined.
The reference is the state-manifold dimension 2^(n+1)-2. The full ceiling is min(p, 2^(n+1)-2); p is the n_params column of the record.

Redundancy R = 1 - rank/p is reported with the rank (Haug Table I). At shallow depth R is design redundancy; once the rank saturates the manifold at larger depth, R also counts over-parameterisation, so read R at d = 1 for the redundancy of the generators alone.
The encoder input is held fixed, so P3 describes the ansatz and not the encoder.

P4.name: Dynamical Lie algebra dimension
P4.unit: dimension of the reachable algebra; full su(2^n) is 4^n - 1
P4.source: Larocca et al., Quantum 6, 824 (2022); barren-plateau scaling from Ragone et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 7172 (2024)
deviations: The generator set of each family is declared in its ansatze/ file. A fixed entangler is represented by the non-trivial Pauli terms of its generator; for the CNOT chain of A1 this is Z_q X_(q+1), which is also the native cross-resonance generator of the Kandala hardware.

The Lie-closure dimension is invariant under the fixed single-qubit Clifford gates of a circuit, so those gates are not dressed onto the generators. Only the entangling structure they induce is included.
The dimension is exact only up to DIM_CAP. Above it the value is a lower bound, marked by dla_capped, because a full algebra is exponential in n.

P5.name: Parameter count
P5.unit: number of variational angles M = n_params(n, d)
P5.source: Circuit definition; used as the denominator of Haug's redundancy R = (M - D_C) / M, Haug, Bharti & Kim, PRX Quantum 2, 040309 (2021)
deviations: P5 is a cost control, not a capability. It is reported so that P3's effective dimension can be normalised into a redundancy.
The value duplicates the n_params column that every record already carries; it is exposed as a metric so it can be run and correlated on its own.

P6.name: Two-qubit gate count
P6.unit: number of two-qubit gates on the tape
P6.source: Circuit definition; two-qubit gates are the dominant NISQ error source
deviations: P6 is a cost control, not a capability. It stands in for the hardware error budget, since two-qubit gates dominate NISQ error rates.

The count is read from the tape, so it reflects the CNOT chain of A1, the CNOT rings of A2 and A3 and the CRZ ring plus cups of A4 exactly as apply() queues them, with no separate formula to keep in step.

A1.name: HEA (Kandala 2017)
deviations: Entangler is a linear CNOT chain. The paper uses hardware-native cross-resonance gates.

A2.name: SEL + classical embedding (Schuld 2020)
A2.source: Schuld et al., Phys. Rev. A 101, 032308 (2020)
deviations: The embedding vector is fixed, not swept over a dataset. P1 therefore measures the ansatz, not the encoder.
Ring range grows as (layer mod (n-1)) + 1, as in PennyLane StronglyEntanglingLayers.

A3.name: Data re-uploading (Perez-Salinas 2020)
deviations: The paper is single-qubit. The CNOT ring between repeats is an extension, needed to make the multi-qubit grid meaningful.
The input is fixed, as in A2, so P1 measures the ansatz.
Only n = 4 is inside the declared protocol. Other widths are controls.

A4.name: DisCoCat sentence circuit (pre-contraction)
A4.source: Coecke et al. arXiv:2005.04147; Kartsaklis et al. arXiv:2110.04236
deviations: CUPS ARE NOT POST-SELECTED. Only the CNOT and H are queued. This is an upper bound on the contracted sentence circuit.
The parse is a fixed alternating noun-verb template, not a real parser output. Sentence length maps to n as one qubit per word.
Word boxes are IQP-style (H layer + CRZ ring), as in the lambeq IQPAnsatz, not the paper's abstract word boxes.
